title: Electrolytes, Sports Drinks, and Sugar-Free Hydration
lessons: The player first considers Liquid I.V. because the brand claims its hydration formulas provide more electrolytes than a leading sports drink.
The player likes the format but has switched from the original formula to a sugar-free Hydration Multiplier.

text: Late gym, your water bottle, a packet someone left on the bench. The front says it has three times the electrolytes of the leading sports drink.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Three times the electrolytes sounds like a number built for a shelf label.

entry-first-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: It's specific on purpose. It's three times a particular sports drink. Not three times water. Not three times nothing. I'd rather be checked on the real number than trusted on the big one.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the comparison is the actual claim, not the big hydration promise doing all the talking.

entry-first-4.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Yes. The headline's mine, but the comparison's the part you can go check. Go check it.

choice-first.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You're going to tear the packet open or put it back. Which?

choices.text: I like knowing what you're actually trying to do.
I want to know what that electrolyte number costs me in sugar.
I don't need a performance claim shouted at me after every workout.

first-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Good. Practical is why I get invited into the gym bag. I'd like to be liked for other reasons, but I'll start there.

first-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Keep reading down the label, then. Past the comparison line. If sodium or sugar is your worry, that's where it lives, and it's in bigger numbers than you'd guess.

first-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Fair. A lot of workouts end perfectly fine with tap water and nothing else. I'd be lying if I said otherwise.
You still keep a packet in your gym bag. It's the sugar-free one now.

entry-return-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You kept a packet in your bag. You changed what's in it.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: I liked the convenience. I didn't want the sugar every night I trained.

entry-return-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Then Sugar-Free is the one you actually wanted. Same packet, same little pour into the bottle, one less thing to argue with.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: Same little routine, less arguing with the label at ten at night.

entry-return-5.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: That's the kind of boring compatibility I actually want to be known for.

choice-return.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: So are we good, or is the label still on trial?

choices.text: I like that I didn't have to leave you to fix that.
I still want to know exactly what sweetener replaced the sugar.
I'd rather skip flavored hydration after a workout entirely.

return-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Good. Then use that one and stop thinking about it. That's the nicest thing you can do for me.

return-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Then read it. Sugar-free means no sugar. It doesn't mean nothing. You should know what's in there.

return-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: That's a real option too. I don't need to win every bottle of water in this gym. Some of them, sure.
